title: The Solubility of Carbon Dioxide and Nitrous Oxide in Aqueous Salt Solutions
authors: Aaron E. Markham and Kenneth A. Kobe
journal: J. Am. Chem. Soc. 63 (2), 449-454 (this PDF begins with the last page of another article, p. 449, on specific volumes of NaCl and NaBr solutions; the Markham-Kobe paper starts on p. 449 bottom and runs to p. 454)
experimental_method: Ostwald-type volumetric method: a measured volume of gas at 760 mm partial pressure is shaken with a measured quantity of gas-free solution in a two-bulb oscillating flask in a thermostat, and the volume remaining in a mercury buret is read by cathetometer.
uncertainties_stated: Probable experimental error 0.2 %; temperature variation up to 0.1 C at 0.2 C and never more than 0.03 C at other temperatures; pure-water average deviations of alpha x 1000 listed in Table I.
quality_remarks: Authors state solubilities as measured are low by several hundredths, possibly up to 0.1 %, from solution expansion; gas impurity (CO2 99.8 %, N2O 99.7 %) not corrected; vapour pressures of solutions taken from the literature; ideal-gas molar volume used for the Bunsen coefficient although apparent CO2 molecular weight deviates 0.2 % from ideal. Some footnoted cells (a, b, c) are at salt molalities different from the m column. Table values transcribed from the scan; the OCR text layer was consistent with the image.
